clue.text: Public school boy boxing second European

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it on all sides, so one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a pupil at Eton, the famous English public school
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A schoolboy from a smart school takes up boxing against a European opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'public school' is an expensive private school; Eton is the best known, and its pupils are Etonians. ETONIAN holds S to give ESTONIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Estonia, the Baltic country, is a European by nationality and continent.

clue.text: Queen excused from drill duty

indicators.note: someone excused from a task is let off it, so these letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: a drill is a practice routine

explanation.surface: The monarch gets let off having to take part in military drill.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ER out of EXERCISE and EXCISE is left; 'duty' is a tax, not a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a tax charged on goods such as alcohol and tobacco, and a tax of that kind is called a duty.

clue.text: Publishers in support of hairpiece

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A publishing house backs a campaign for wigs.
explanation.walkthrough: OUP is Oxford University Press; a golf tee is what supports the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A toupee is a small wig worn to cover a bald patch, a common kind of hairpiece.

clue.text: Number after number that's lower?

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
read as numb-er, something that numbs: an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A puzzle about one figure coming after another and ending up smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Number' is a thing that makes you numb, the anaesthetic ether; 'after' puts it behind the second number, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old adjective meaning lower or underneath, as in the nether regions of a place.

clue.text: Make better meal, or I eat junk!

indicators.note: junk is rubbish thrown together, so these letters are a jumble to be put in order

explanation.surface: A demand to improve dinner before the speaker is reduced to eating junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate a situation is to improve it, a formal synonym for making something better.

clue.text: Extremely funny joke for southern elite?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the cream of society is its best

explanation.surface: A really good gag aimed at a posh audience in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something hilarious is called a scream, as in 'that sketch was an absolute scream'.

clue.text: Committee chap at party for a military unit

explanation.surface: A committee member at a party argues the case for an army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a small force of soldiers trained for raids, a type of military unit.

clue.text: Mule is skidding on oily mixture

indicators.note: something skidding slides out of control, so these letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A mule slipping about on a greasy patch.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulsion is a blend of oil and water held as fine droplets, so it is an oily mixture; the word also covers paint.

clue.text: Fellow introducing duck to plant

explanation.surface: A man shows a duck a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean herb with a forked root, famous in folklore, and so a plant.

clue.text: Dispatch rider to take Tibetan leader to member of the royal household

indicators.note: the leader of a word is at its front, so only the opening letter is wanted
to take something in is to hold it, so the one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A motorcycle messenger is sent to fetch a Tibetan lama to see a palace official.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is someone who attends a monarch at court, an official in the royal household.

clue.text: Setter's dog facing new attack

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so setter's = I'm
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker's dog is up against a fresh assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves in the third person, so 'Setter's' reads as I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn someone's motives is to challenge or attack them verbally, especially their honesty.

clue.text: Shed meeting wicked, wicked woman

blocks.note: the first of the pair, a synonym

explanation.surface: A garden shed gets a visit from a cruel woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is not a typo: the first 'wicked' is wordplay, the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a malicious, spiteful woman, so it names a wicked woman.

clue.text: Cable carried by rickshaw service

indicators.note: what is carried by something sits within it, so the letters are inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: A wire being transported by a rickshaw company.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or steel cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Ran into antique damaged by a period of isolation

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bumped into an old piece of furniture and broke it during lockdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a time kept apart from others to stop the spread of disease, a spell of enforced isolation.

clue.text: Preparation of crushed ginger's last to go into pot for cooking

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one wanted here
going into something means sitting inside it, so the single letter is placed within the vessel

blocks.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe step: crushed ginger goes into the pan to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger's last' reads like a final step of the recipe, but it means only the final letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundwork is the basic preliminary work done before a project, its preparation.

clue.text: Lawyer mostly drinking American liqueur

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word is cut short by its last letter
a drinker takes something in, so the short piece goes inside

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A barrister who drinks most of an American's liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVOCATE loses its E to give ADVOCAT, and A goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy, a sweet drink served in small glasses.

clue.text: Injured goblin getting a bumpy ride

indicators.note: a bumpy ride jolts things about, so these letters are jostled into a new order

explanation.surface: A little goblin gets hurt after a rough journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means weakened or damaged in function, as an injured limb is.

clue.text: Dangerous situation created by papers about yearly meeting

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Documents tabled at the annual meeting have stirred up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A quagmire is literally a bog, and figuratively a hazardous, awkward situation that is hard to escape.

clue.text: RAF squadron's cleaners seen accepting a degree

indicators.note: a word accepting others takes them in, so they sit inside it

explanation.surface: Cleaners working for an air force unit are spotted taking a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is a medical degree. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dambusters is the nickname of the RAF's 617 Squadron, which bombed German dams in 1943.

clue.text: Fuss with undergarment

blocks.note: second meaning: a pad or frame worn under a Victorian skirt to puff out the back

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a complaint about underwear, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hurried, fussy activity, and also a frame worn beneath a long skirt to hold it out behind.

clue.text: Denied access to somewhere to drink claret?

explanation.surface: Someone turned away from a wine bar while wanting a glass of claret.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is red Bordeaux wine; the question mark flags the indirect clue to RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be barred from a place is to be banned from entering it.

clue.text: Note match fix!

blocks.note: the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A newspaper-style exclamation about a match being fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, and fix is a common everyday synonym.

clue.text: Old variety of fruit

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An heirloom kind of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit, so it is a straightforward example of fruit.

clue.text: Cruel article found in Bury

indicators.note: what is found in something lies within it, so the short word goes inside

explanation.surface: A harsh newspaper story discovered in the town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, a town near Manchester, is capitalised to hide the verb; the 'article' is a grammar word, not a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion and causing suffering, so it is a synonym of cruel.

clue.text: Fearful African given assistance

explanation.surface: A frightened African is offered help.
explanation.definitionFit: To be afraid is to be scared or full of fear, so fearful is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Schedule time to get to grips with one source of food poisoning

indicators.note: getting to grips with something means grasping it, so the word holds the next piece

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Planning time to deal with one cause of a stomach bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a bacterium found in soft cheese and chilled foods that causes listeriosis, a form of food poisoning.

clue.text: Commitments interrupted by inspector's orders

indicators.note: a thing interrupted has something break into its middle, so the second piece goes inside

explanation.surface: A police inspector's instructions break into someone's prior engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' is a verb here: puts in order. The 's means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy a room is to put it in order, so tidies works as the verb orders.

clue.text: Guardian editor returned with electric guitar

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: a Fender is a famous make of electric guitar

explanation.surface: A Guardian newspaper editor comes back carrying an electric guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper, but it is the definition: a protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender protects someone or something from attack, so is a guardian.
